parts.note: a prop is something that holds a thing up

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of also are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sorts out a scheme with backing as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is a scheme put forward, so it is a synonym of a plan.

definitions.meaning: to ... a law or act is to revoke it
read as a peal rung a second time, as an encore would be

explanation.surface: Calling off the bellringers' repeat performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Repealing an act withdraws it, which is cancelling it; the question mark flags the punning re-peal.

indicators.note: developing means the letters of a rich part grow into a different shape

explanation.surface: A company founder building up a wealthy division.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriarch is the male founder or father figure of a family or tribe.

clue.text: Joint second team in the Olympics, maybe

parts.note: the Olympic runner-up wins silver, so silver stands for second place
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A team sharing second place at the Olympic Games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the Olympics, maybe' tells you second means the silver medal. 'Joint' looks like 'shared', but silverside is a joint of beef from the hindquarter, popular in Britain for roasting or salting.
explanation.definitionFit: Silverside is a cut of beef from the outer thigh, so it is an example of a butcher's joint.

definitions.meaning: pale in colour, as fair hair or skin is
the brightness that lets us see

explanation.definitionFit: Light hair is fair hair, and light is also the brightness from a lamp or the sun.

definitions.meaning: open land the whole community may use

explanation.definitionFit: Something common happens often, and a village common is public ground open to everyone.

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of chintzy

explanation.surface: A town whose decor is a bit tacky.
explanation.definitionFit: A municipality is a town or city with its own local government; 'perhaps' marks a city as one example.

clue.text: I'm standing up twice before Concorde's first take off

indicators.note: before puts the doubled pair ahead of the next piece
twice says the reversed pair is written two times
in a down entry, standing up means the letters run upwards, so they read backwards

parts.note: the clue word read without its apostrophe

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of Concorde's

explanation.surface: Someone excitedly rising from their seat as Concorde takes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' looks like Concorde leaving the runway, but here it means imitate someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to impersonate them, which is what a mimic does.

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of honestly are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Something set up with apparent honesty but in secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on the sly means doing it secretly, without others noticing.

indicators.note: unending means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a rash shows up as spots on the skin

explanation.surface: Noticing a rash that won't go away.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice or catch sight of it.

clue.text: Run off with nameless convict? That's allowed

parts.note: to leg it is British slang for running away

indicators.note: nameless means N, short for name, is taken out

parts.note: an inmate is a prisoner

explanation.surface: A prison break with an unnamed inmate, jokingly asked whether it is permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leg it' is British slang for running away fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something legitimate is permitted by law or rules, which is what allowed means.

parts.note: manifest means plain, open to view
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: An openly declared stance of a political circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto sets out a political party's declared policies, its official line.

definitions.meaning: British slang for a prison warder

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are British slang: a screw is a prison guard, and a screw was a wage, as in 'earning a good screw'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a warder is a screw, and one's salary is also called a screw.

parts.note: a sore spot is tender
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour place names

explanation.surface: Someone with a painful head being treated kindly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a headland, not a part of the body: NESS appears in British place names such as Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderness is kindness and care, the gentle way of handling someone.

indicators.note: doubled says the word is from the clue is written a second time

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: Credit is doubled to cope with an urgent situation.
explanation.walkthrough: In accounting, CR is the standard abbreviation for credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a time of acute danger or difficulty, which an emergency is.

clue.text: Presumed to hold an amount of money

indicators.note: to hold means the answer sits inside the word presumed

explanation.surface: Someone assumed to be carrying a quantity of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is a quantity of money, as in 'a large sum'.

clue.text: Preserve cooked meal doctor's tucking into

indicators.note: tucking into says the doctor goes inside the mixed-up letters
cooked says the letters of meal are mixed up

parts.note: MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine, so a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor eating a prepared meal, kept for later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' looks like eating, but it is the container signal; 'cooked' is the anagram signal and 'doctor's' is doctor is.
explanation.definitionFit: To embalm a body is to preserve it from decay.

clue.text: Having made a deal, lawyers profited

parts.note: the Bar is the collective name for barristers
gained means made a profit

explanation.surface: Lawyers who struck a deal and came out ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Having bargained, one has haggled and agreed terms, which is making a deal.

indicators.note: to shake says the letters of card sure are jumbled

explanation.surface: A card that is sure to rattle the champion.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader campaigns vigorously for a cause, so champions it.

indicators.note: in says the answer is found inside the words porch, I deposited

explanation.surface: Someone leaving something in the porch, a large flower, as it turns out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' might suggest a blunder or a loaf of bread, but here it is simply something that blooms, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchid is a flowering plant, so in crossword terms it is a bloomer.

indicators.note: to face means the first piece stands in front of the second

parts.note: a mode is a way of doing something
RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A fresh method of tackling a service.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means of the present day, recent rather than old, which is new.

clue.text: In France, she's overwhelmed by part that's shot

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the French word is enclosed within the other piece

parts.note: elle is French for she

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman overcome by the role she has been cast in.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot in the sense of ammunition is small pellets, as fired from a shotgun.

clue.text: Posh son will have time for established procedure

parts.note: U means upper-class
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An upper-class son will be given time for the customary way of doing things.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from 1950s British debate on 'U and non-U' speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is customary practice, the habitual or accepted way something is done.

indicators.note: half-hearted means one of the two central letters is lost

parts.note: a gallop is a fast run

explanation.surface: A lacklustre jog that ends in a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A galop is a lively nineteenth-century ballroom dance in two-four time.

parts.note: read literally, one who watches the night sky rather than a guard on night duty

explanation.walkthrough: A night-watchman is a security guard, and in cricket a lower-order batter sent in late; the question mark points to someone watching the night sky instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A stargazer looks at the stars, which come out at night, so watches the night.

clue.text: Finally accept inclination to provide public transport

definitions.note: a tramp is a long walk, the means of getting about open to everyone

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of accept

parts.note: a ramp is an inclined slope

explanation.surface: Accepting at last a slope built for buses and trains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'public transport' looks like buses and trams, but it is a cryptic definition: a tramp, a long trudge on foot, is transport anyone can use.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a long, tiring walk, and walking is the travel available to every member of the public.

parts.note: wee is Scottish for tiny
D is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A tiny unwanted plant has died.
explanation.definitionFit: A weed is any plant growing where it is not wanted.

parts.note: an adult is a grown-up
E is the fifth letter, so the fifth grade of quality
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: A grown-up demeaned by a shoddy accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fifth-rate' gives E as a grade, like A for first-rate, then 'charge' gives RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulterate is to make something impure by adding inferior matter, which lowers or debases it.

indicators.note: returned says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words hospital lunch

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A patient sent home from a hospital meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' looks like a sick person, but it is the adjective meaning void; 'from' signals the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Null as in 'null and void' means having no legal force, so not valid.

indicators.note: after means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a trip is a short holiday
OD is the banking abbreviation for overdrawn

explanation.surface: Someone left in the red after a holiday needing help.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripod is a three-legged stand holding a camera steady, so a support.

clue.text: Spotted a careless mark with a later day

indicators.note: careless suggests the letters of spotted a are set down sloppily in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone spotted making a sloppy mark with the next day's date.
explanation.definitionFit: To postdate a cheque or document is to write on it a date after the actual one.
